step1_analysis.description: A high-speed, low-power rail-to-rail buffer amplifier designed for LCD column driving. It utilizes complementary differential input pairs to achieve rail-to-rail operation and includes an inversion controller for polarity switching.

paper_reference.title: A High-Speed Low-Power Rail-to-Rail Column Driver for AMLCD Application

power.description: Total DC power consumption of the column driver.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_total. With VDD=1.8V and typical bias currents of ~10-20uA per stage.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted for SKY130 1.8V supply. The static power is dominated by the tail current sources and the second-stage bias.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = gm / (2 * pi * C_load). With C_load = 30pF and gm ~ 1mA/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Driving a heavy 30pF load significantly reduces bandwidth. The 162MHz reported in the paper might be unloaded or with a smaller capacitance.

rise_time.description: Time required for the output to transition from 10% to 90% of its final value.

paper_reported.value: Not explicitly listed, but implied high-speed.

sky130_expected.calculation: t_rise ~ 2.2 * R_out * C_load or Slew Rate limited (I_tail / C_load).
sky130_expected.reasoning: With a 30pF load and typical tail currents, slew rate limiting will dominate the large-signal rise time.

fall_time.description: Time required for the output to transition from 90% to 10% of its final value.

sky130_expected.calculation: t_fall ~ 2.2 * R_out * C_load or Slew Rate limited.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Similar to rise time, heavily dependent on the pull-down capability of the output stage and the 30pF load.

sky130_expected.calculation: V_max = VDD - V_dsat of the pull-up PMOS.
sky130_expected.reasoning: As a rail-to-rail buffer, it should swing very close to the 1.8V supply rail.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC bandwidth, and transient response (rise/fall times, voltage swing) of the rail-to-rail column driver. Includes a workaround for a floating node (N14) and a passive pull-down to compensate for extraction artifacts in the complementary stage.
